report: Louise required full assistance with washing this morning. During the bathing process, a 5cm lesion was found on her left buttock with signs of infection. A swab was obtained and wound management was initiated. Current treatment includes Inadine and Leukomed dressings. Awaiting Tissue Viability Nurse consultation.

Roland experienced significant breathlessness after brief activity today and reported increased back pain during the morning shift. Pain relief medication was administered with minimal effect. He ate sparingly, requiring encouragement and adapted cutlery. The family has been notified, and medication review has been requested.

Martha seemed more confused and agitated than usual, wandering restlessly during the night. She declined her evening meal, showing signs of nausea and mild diarrhoea. Hydration maintained, though intake is monitored closely. Oral medications given with difficulty. Care plan discussions arranged for tomorrow.

Eleanor was assisted with teeth brushing and dressing this morning. A new pressure ulcer was observed on her right heel, measuring approximately 3cm, with some signs of redness and skin breakdown. Wound dressing applied and elevation of the limb maintained. Awaiting review from wound care specialist.

Frank had a restless night, frequently calling out due to chest tightness and discomfort. Required full assistance with transfers to and from bed. His appetite has decreased dramatically, and he appeared very fatigued. Palliative care team to reassess pain management strategy, as current measures are ineffective.

Louise was assisted with a bed bath today. She appeared uncomfortable and reported mild back pain during the process. She has a stage 2 pressure ulcer on her left heel, which was cleaned and dressed with Inadine and Mepilex Border. She expressed confusion when asked simple questions and seemed distracted throughout the morning.

Tom was encouraged to eat his lunch but required full assistance and adapted cutlery due to his severe arthritis. He managed to consume about half of his meal and drank 200ml of fluids. He complained of abdominal tightness and was given his prescribed medication for ongoing nausea. He was resting quietly afterward but appeared agitated when repositioned in his wheelchair.

Eleanor participated in brief social activity, browsing through a magazine with assistance. She was more withdrawn than usual and did not engage with staff or fellow residents. Eleanor has extensive oedema in her lower limbs, and her skin shows redness and slight peeling. Her family visited, and a care plan discussion focused on managing her increasing fatigue and pain.

Roger was restless and attempted to get out of bed multiple times during the night. He reported persistent thigh pain and had difficulty finding a comfortable position, leading to agitation. The night staff noticed that his dental prostheses were not cleaned properly, causing discomfort. Additional assistance was given to ensure proper oral hygiene.

Marian required assistance with brushing teeth and general hygiene. She seemed disoriented this morning, showing subtle signs of increased confusion. Marian complained of chest tightness and was monitored closely; her oxygen levels were within normal range. Both family and staff are concerned about her worsening apathy and ongoing lethargy.

Louise was visited by the GP today for control of her pain, as she has been experiencing increasing discomfort. She required full assistance with eating her breakfast due to weakness and received a fortifying shake to supplement her nutrition. Visitors were limited, contributing to her slight agitation and feelings of loneliness. Staff ensured her hydration list was updated appropriately. She experienced slight breathlessness today, and medications were adjusted accordingly.

Phillip had difficulty sleeping and was restless through the night, requiring repositioning multiple times to enhance comfort and prevent pressure sores. He was partially assisted with his morning wash and wore his oxygen mask without complaints. During lunch, he needed encouragement and the use of adapted cutlery to finish his meal, but he appeared more apathic than usual. A review of his pain management and palliative care plan was discussed.

Maria presented with increased nausea and required frequent antiemetic medication throughout the day. She had a wound dressing changed on a chronic ulcer on her heel, which showed signs of moderate infection. Physical therapy aided her in a short walk to the common area where she barely interacted with other residents, her usual sociable demeanor notably diminished. Pain relief measures and additional nutritional supplements have been put in place.

Jonathan received assistance with his evening hygiene routine after a brief episode of incontinence. He showed signs of confusion during supper, needing close supervision to avoid a choking incident. Interaction with fellow residents was minimal as he was mainly confined to his wheelchair due to severe leg pain. Staff logged his discomfort and kidney function monitoring plans were discussed due to recurring issues.

Eleanor's family visited today but noted her increased apathy and inability to recognize them, which was distressing. She struggled with breathlessness and received nebulizer treatment and oxygen supplement throughout the day. A minor fall occurred while transferring from bed to a wheelchair in the evening; fortunately, she sustained no injury. Pain management continues to be adjusted to keep her comfortable.

This morning, Arthur received help with his daily wash. Noticed an 8cm pressure ulcer on his right heel, surrounded by redness and some exudate present. A sample swab was taken, and wound management protocol initiated. The site is currently covered with Aquacel dressing. The Dermatology team has been informed for further evaluation. Progressively, Arthur showed discomfort while trying to eat breakfast, displaying difficulty in swallowing. Encouragement provided, and alternative textures considered.

Maggie experienced significant restlessness last night, wandering the halls several times and exhibiting signs of confusion. She was gently guided back to her room and assisted into a comfortable sleeping position. Maggie's water intake has been suboptimal; nurses encouraged hydration throughout the day, documenting every attempt. In response, she showed irritation when offered help with dental hygiene in the morning. Coordination with the care plan team suggested adjusting her bedtime routine.

This afternoon, George engaged minimally during the scheduled group activity, appearing apathetic and withdrawn. Assistance was provided in grooming, yet he expressed discomfort due to ongoing back pain. Mild analgesics administered, observing for effects. Family updated on George's condition and mood fluctuations. Subsequently, required full help during meal times, displaying no interest in self-eating despite adaptive cutlery and supportive prompts.

Linda showed signs of agitation through the night, leading to several phone attempts to her family. Requiring frequent repositioning due to complaints of hip pain, analgesics were administered as per palliative guidelines. Noted swelling in lower extremities, suggesting possible fluid retention. Immediate measures taken to elevate her legs while awaiting physician review. Nutrition intake closely monitored; a noticeable decline was documented.

Despite Irene attending a brief social interaction with other residents, she remained largely unresponsive and exhibited confusion. Observed struggling with independent mobility, requiring frequent support with fall-prevention strategies. Nursing team identified multiple minor skin tears necessitating gentle cleaning and dressings. Engaged in a discussion for potential adjustments to her palliative care regimen, involving input from the family regarding comfort measures.

Louise was provided with full assistance for her morning routines, including washing and dressing. She continues to experience significant pain from her left shoulder. Pain relief medication has been administered, however, it remains a responsibility to monitor and record her comfort levels. Visited by her daughter today, Louise remained in good spirits during the visit.

John needed substantial help with his breakfast today, as his ability to manage utensils has declined. He appeared very fatigued and did not consume much. He seemed more disoriented than usual and expressed discomfort in his lower abdomen. A bowel chart has been initiated to monitor his progress, and hydration levels are being closely watched.

Maria struggled significantly with mobility today, requiring support from both a walking aid and assistance from two carers to transfer from her bed to her wheelchair. She reported severe back pain during these movements. A scheduled appointment with a physiotherapist has been noted to explore better pain management options.

Doris was restless throughout the night, frequently calling for assistance and appearing anxious. She wandered the halls in a confused state, requiring continual redirection back to her room. Morning assessment revealed signs of dehydration; fluids have been pushed, and intake will be closely monitored.

Norman showed increased shortness of breath and required the use of supplemental oxygen throughout the day. He was predominantly bedridden, with expressions of general fatigue and some chest tightness. Family requested an update on his condition; palliative care team notified for further assessment.
